public import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Erdős Problem 400

*Reference:* [erdosproblems.com/400](https://www.erdosproblems.com/400)
-/

@[expose] public section

open Nat Filter Finset
open scoped Asymptotics Topology

namespace Erdos400

/--
For any $k\geq 2$ let $g_k(n)$ denote the maximum value of $(a_1+\cdots+a_k)-n$
where $a_1,\ldots,a_k$ are integers such that $a_1!\cdots a_k! \mid n!$.
-/
noncomputable def g (k n : ℕ) : ℕ :=
  sSup { ((∑ i, a i) - n) | (a : Fin k → ℕ) (_ : (∏ i, (a i) !) ∣ n !) }

/--
Can one show that $\sum_{n\leq x}g_k(n) \sim c_k x\log x$ for some constant $c_k$?
-/
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_400.parts.i :
    answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ᵉ (k ≥ 2), ∃ c : ℝ,
      (fun x : ℕ ↦ (∑ n ∈ Icc 1 x, (g k n : ℝ))) ~[atTop]
      (fun x : ℕ ↦ c * x * Real.log x) := by
  sorry

/--
Is it true that there is a constant $c_k$ such that for almost all $n < x$ we have
$g_k(n)=c_k\log x+o(\log x)$?
-/
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_400.parts.ii :
    answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ᵉ (k ≥ 2), ∃ c : ℝ, ∀ ε > 0,
      Tendsto (fun x : ℕ ↦
        (((Icc 1 x).filter (fun n ↦
          |(g k n : ℝ) - c * Real.log x| ≤ ε * Real.log x)).card : ℝ) / x)
        atTop (𝓝 1) := by
  sorry

/--
Erdős and Graham write that it is easy to show that $g_k(n) \ll_k \log n$ always, but the best
possible constant is unknown.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_400.variants.upper_bound (k : ℕ) (hk : k ≥ 2) :
    (fun n : ℕ ↦ (g k n : ℝ)) ≪ (fun n : ℕ ↦ Real.log (n : ℝ)) := by
  sorry


/-- For $k \ge 2$, $g_k(n) > 0$. We show this by choosing $a = (n, 1, 0, \ldots, 0)$. -/
@[category test, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_400.variants.g_pos (k n : ℕ) (h: k ≥ 2) : 0 < g k n := by
  obtain ⟨k', rfl⟩ : ∃ k', k = k' + 2 := ⟨k - 2, by omega⟩
  simp only [g]
  -- Witness: a(0) = n, a(1) = 1, a(i) = 0 for i ≥ 2
  set a : Fin (k' + 2) → ℕ := fun i =>
    if (i : ℕ) = 0 then n else if (i : ℕ) = 1 then 1 else 0 with ha_def
  have h_prod : ∏ i : Fin (k' + 2), (a i)! = n ! := by
    rw [Fin.prod_univ_succ]; simp [ha_def]
    rw [Fin.prod_univ_succ]; simp
  have h_sum : ∑ i : Fin (k' + 2), a i = n + 1 := by
    rw [Fin.sum_univ_succ]; simp [ha_def]
  -- 1 is in the set
  have hmem : 1 ∈ {(∑ i, b i) - n | (b : Fin (k' + 2) → ℕ) (_ : ∏ i, (b i)! ∣ n !)} :=
    ⟨a, h_prod ▸ dvd_refl n !, by omega⟩
  -- The set is bounded above by (k'+2) * n!
  have hbdd : BddAbove {(∑ i, b i) - n | (b : Fin (k' + 2) → ℕ) (_ : ∏ i, (b i)! ∣ n !)} := by
    refine ⟨(k' + 2) * n !, ?_⟩
    rintro x ⟨b, hb, rfl⟩
    calc (∑ i, b i) - n
        ≤ ∑ i, b i := Nat.sub_le _ _
      _ ≤ ∑ i : Fin (k' + 2), (b i)! :=
          Finset.sum_le_sum fun i _ => Nat.self_le_factorial _
      _ ≤ Finset.univ.card • n ! := by
          apply Finset.sum_le_card_nsmul; intro i _
          exact le_trans (Finset.single_le_prod' (fun j _ =>
            Nat.one_le_iff_ne_zero.mpr (Nat.factorial_ne_zero _))
            (Finset.mem_univ i)) (Nat.le_of_dvd (Nat.factorial_pos n) hb)
      _ = (k' + 2) * n ! := by simp [smul_eq_mul]
  exact Nat.lt_of_lt_of_le Nat.one_pos (le_csSup hbdd hmem)

end Erdos400

reformulations.difference: Uses an ℕ-valued supremum and truncated subtraction, with zero permitted among the factorial arguments, instead of an ordinary integer-valued maximum.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Every admissible coordinate satisfies a_i ≤ max n 1, so the admissible value set is nonempty and bounded and its supremum is attained. For k ≥ 2, the tuple (n,1,0,…) gives positive excess, so truncating negative excesses does not change the maximum. Replacing zero coordinates by 1 preserves the factorial product and increases the sum, so allowing zero also leaves the maximum over positive coordinates unchanged. In /workspace/review/scratch.lean, positive_integer_maximum_iff proves that an integer z is this ordinary maximum over positive tuples iff z = (Erdos400.g k n : ℤ), without sorry.

reformulations.difference: Expresses the almost-all little-o assertion through the proportions of ε-good indices tending to 1, and includes the endpoint n = x.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: For positive integer x, good and exceptional counts add to x. Thus the Lean condition is equivalent to requiring, for every ε > 0, that #{1 ≤ n ≤ x : |g_k(n) − c log x| > ε log x} = o(x). This count equivalence is proved by partII_exceptional_count in the scratch file. A diagonal choice ε(x) → 0 gives the source's o(log x) error outside o(x) exceptions; conversely that formulation immediately implies every fixed-ε condition. Including n = x changes the count by at most one. Restricting x to natural numbers is harmless by comparison with floor(x). The full diagonalization and endpoint/real-parameter equivalences were not formalized in Lean.

review.notes: Checked all five declarations. The source still marks the two questions open; the recent literature supplies partial bounds, not their requested asymptotics. The solved upper-bound tag agrees with the source. Its atTop Big-O formulation permits constants depending on k and is the usual Vinogradov bound; finite initial values do not affect it. Lean checks established an executable finite-search version equal to g and evaluated k = 0,…,4 and n = 0,…,10. They also proved that part (i)'s asymptotic constant must be positive, so allowing arbitrary real c introduces no zero-constant escape. The supplied g_pos proof and all completed scratch certificates have no sorryAx dependency. Division by zero and log 0/log 1 affect only initial terms of the limits.
